question: What Earthrise interval is independently supported by the fixed Orion SAW Cam 3 sequence, and does the official OTR observation availability window contain or overlap it?
decisive_invariant: Only a physical interval derived from hash-pinned fixed-camera images and their PDS4 timestamps may be compared with the OTR availability window; transcript wording and OTR endpoints may not define the image states.
claim_ceiling: Window coverage or non-coverage for this one Earthrise sequence. No boundary-delay, causal, operational-impact, or mission-wide claim.

environment.runtime_contract: Python 3 standard library only for scored verification.
environment.timezone_contract: All timestamps are UTC. No local-time conversion is permitted.

admission_checks: Every scored source file matches its frozen byte length and SHA-256.
Each browse label binds its JPEG to the corresponding raw-image logical identifier.
Every timestamp is read from a PDS4 raw-image data label and matches the frozen visual classification.
Frames are in strict 30-second cadence and the state sequence is NOT_VISIBLE, PARTIAL, PARTIAL, PARTIAL, FULL_CLEAR, FULL_CLEAR.
The full-clear classification is corroborated by a following stable frame.
The OTR values are read from the pinned source and retained as availability-window endpoints.

spice_branch.reason: NASA PDS lists the Artemis II SPICE actual release as TBD; no archive bundle was available to pin.

next_step_logic.recommended: Run the same small, fixed-camera image-state coverage test for Earthset, Sunset, and Sunrise before any broad archive analysis.
next_step_logic.why: Earthrise now establishes a real non-overlap, but one event cannot distinguish an isolated planning choice from a repeated window-placement pattern.
next_step_logic.alternative: Re-attest Earthrise with the Artemis II SPICE bundle after NASA publishes an actual release.
next_step_logic.fallback: If the other event families do not reproduce the relation, pivot to Stage 3 target execution and attention allocation rather than widening the timing claim.
